previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with a history of end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, and diabetes was admitted for acute shortness of breath that began suddenly while watching television. She presented with hypertensive urgency and signs of pulmonary edema. EMS initiated CPAP and nitroglycerin, which improved her symptoms. In the hospital, she was managed with oxygen support, antihypertensives, and scheduled hemodialysis, which led to significant improvement in her respiratory status and fluid balance. A urine culture from a prior admission grew Klebsiella, prompting a short course of oral antibiotics. She was discharged home with nursing services, new instructions for a Sunday dose of Imdur to prevent interdialytic fluid overload, and education on medication adherence, fluid restriction, and infection monitoring.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with CHF.

Single AP chest radiograph compared to ___, shows increasing
bilateral perihilar opacities and small pleural efffusions compatible with
worsening CHF. Again as superimposed basilar process such as aspiration or
pneumonia cannot be excluded, repeat radiograph after diuresis is recommended.
The cardiomediastinal contour is difficult to evaluate, however, grossly
stable.

IMPRESSION: Worsening CHF.

HISTORY:  Hypoxia.

A single portable radiograph of the chest demonstrates increased opacities
involving both lungs.  Finding demonstrates an airspace pattern and is
markedly improved in the interval when compared to the chest radiograph
obtained eight hours prior.  There is very mild blunting of the right
costophrenic angle.  No pneumothorax.  The cardiomediastinal contour is
unremarkable.  Trachea is midline.

IMPRESSION:

Marked interval improvement in airspace opacity involving both lungs.  The
finding likely represents improving pulmonary edema superimposed on an
interstitial abnormality.  This might be better characterized with CT
examination of the chest.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with recurrent hypoxia.  Please evaluate for
interstitial lung disease.

Comparison is made to the chest radiograph of the same day and chest
radiograph of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial MDCT images of the chest were obtained with no contrast
administration.  Sagittal and coronal reformatted images were then obtained.

CT OF CHEST WITH NO CONTRAST:  Diffuse ground-glass opacities in a
peribronchovascular distribution are noted bilaterally.  These findings
dominantly affect the upper lobes and the perihilar regions.  There is also
diffuse increased septal thickening.  Consolidative changes are noted at the
lung bases, which is more prominent on the left than on the right side.  The
tracheobronchial tree is patent up to the subsegmental levels.  Small
bilateral pleural effusions are noted.  Small amount of fluid is tracking
along the right minor fissure.  Multiple non-pathologically enlarged
mediastinal nodes are noted, the largest one is noted within the anterior
paratracheal location measuring 7 mm.

Diffuse calcification at the origin of aortic arch vessels is noted.  No
pleural or pericardial effusion is noted.  Calcification at the mitral annulus
and carotid arteries are identified.  Incidental note is made of mediastinal
thyroid gland, which contains an 8 mm thyroid nodule in the left lower pole.

The visualized part of the upper abdomen including the adrenal glands and the
liver and spleen appear unremarkable.  Atrophy of both kidneys is noted.

BONE WINDOWS:  No concerning lytic or sclerotic lesions are identified.  Old
healed fracture of the right second, third, and fourth anterior ribs are
noted.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Diffuse septal thickening in association with the alveolar ground-glass
opacities predominantly affecting the upper lobes and the hilar regions is
suggestive of volume overload status and/or heart failure.  The chest findings
can be evaluated after diuresis. Underlying interstitial lung disease cannot
be excluded.

2.  Small bilateral pleural effusion and mild bibasilar atelectasis.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with congestive failure.  Assess for interval
change.

COMPARISON:  CT chest, ___ and chest radiographs, ___.

AP PORTABLE CHEST:  Allowing for differences in patient positioning, overall
there has been no significant change in appearance of the chest.  Bilateral
patchy airspace opacity and increased interstitial markings are compatible
with congestive failure.  Cardiomegaly is stable.  Small bilateral pleural
effusions persist.

IMPRESSION:  Overall, no significant change in findings consistent with edema.
